The mountain village slept under a thick blanket of snow while the river below kept moving between icy banks.
Travelers who crossed the pass spoke of wolves in the forest and of lights that moved above the ridge at night.
The innkeeper fed every guest who arrived and asked little for the warm room at the top of the stairs.
She had lived in the mountains all her life and she trusted the weather more than any almanac.
In spring the meltwater filled the mills and the whole valley smelled of wet grass and wood smoke.
The priest blessed the fields each May and the farmers planted potatoes, beans and barley.
Winter always returned, and the village always waited for it with full cellars and fixed roofs.
